questions.question: 1 million requests per day is roughly how many requests per second on average?
99.99% availability allows roughly how much downtime per year?
In a Dynamo-style store with N replicas, which condition ensures reads see the latest acknowledged write?
questions.explanation: Read and write quorums overlap in at least one replica.

questions.question: Main purpose of consistent hashing with virtual nodes?
options: Minimize data movement when nodes are added or removed, and spread load evenly
questions.explanation: Only about 1/n of keys move when a node changes; virtual nodes smooth out imbalance.

questions.question: You need an event stream that multiple independent consumers can read and replay. Choose:
options: A relational table polled every second
A work queue where messages are deleted once consumed
A log (Kafka / Kinesis / Event Hubs / Pub/Sub)
questions.explanation: Logs retain events; each consumer group tracks its own offset; ordering is per partition.

questions.question: With at-least-once delivery, how do you avoid double-charging a customer?
options: Idempotent consumers using an idempotency key / dedupe table
questions.explanation: End-to-end exactly-once effect = at-least-once delivery + idempotent processing.

questions.question: The 'transactional outbox' pattern solves:
options: Updating a database and publishing an event atomically (no lost or phantom events)
questions.explanation: Write the event to an outbox table in the same DB transaction; a relay publishes it to the broker.

questions.question: When many requests miss the cache for the same hot key at once (stampede), a good mitigation is:
options: Request coalescing (single-flight) and jittered TTLs / stale-while-revalidate
questions.explanation: Let one request rebuild the value while others wait or get stale data; jitter avoids synchronized expiry.

questions.question: For cache-aside, on a write you should usually:
options: Update the cache, then the database
Update both in parallel with no ordering
Never touch the cache; wait for the TTL
Update the database, then delete (invalidate) the cache entry
questions.explanation: Deleting avoids races where a stale value overwrites a fresh one; the next read repopulates it.

questions.question: Which index structure favors write-heavy workloads (used by Cassandra/RocksDB)?
questions.explanation: Writes go to a memtable and are flushed sequentially as SSTables; reads may check several (bloom filters help).

questions.question: CAP theorem: during a network partition, a system must choose between:
questions.explanation: Partitions will happen; the choice is C or A during one. PACELC adds latency vs consistency when there's no partition.

questions.question: Best fit for streaming LLM tokens from server to browser?
questions.explanation: SSE is simple one-way HTTP streaming; WebSockets if you need bi-directional messaging.

questions.question: Offset-based pagination over a feed that receives inserts causes:
options: Duplicated or skipped items between pages; prefer cursor-based pagination
questions.explanation: Cursors (e.g. last seen ID/timestamp) are stable under inserts and scale better.

questions.question: Which estimates the number of distinct users in a huge stream with ~1–2% error in kilobytes of memory?
questions.explanation: Bloom = membership; Count-Min = frequencies; reservoir = uniform sample.

questions.question: News feed for users with 50M followers. Best fan-out strategy?
options: Hybrid: fan-out on write for most users, fan-out on read for celebrities
Fan-out on read for everyone, with no caching
questions.explanation: Pushing one post into 50M timelines is too expensive; merge celebrity posts at read time.

questions.question: In a chat system, how do you guarantee message ordering within a conversation?
options: Per-conversation sequence numbers assigned by the partition owner
questions.explanation: Client clocks skew; global ordering doesn't scale. Order is only needed per conversation.

questions.question: Ride-sharing: drivers send location every 4 s. Where should these updates go?
options: An in-memory geospatial index (geohash/S2/H3 cells), not a write per update to a DB
A relational table with one row per update
questions.explanation: Location updates are high-volume and ephemeral; persist sampled trails asynchronously if needed.

questions.question: Distributed rate limiter backed by Redis: how do you avoid race conditions?
options: Do check-and-decrement atomically (Lua script or atomic INCR with expiry)
Read the counter, then write it in a separate call
Use a local in-memory counter on each server only
questions.explanation: Separate read/write calls race under concurrency.

questions.question: Saga pattern vs 2PC for a multi-service order flow: main advantage of a saga?
options: No blocking coordinator; each step commits locally with compensating actions on failure
questions.explanation: Sagas trade isolation for availability; compensations must be idempotent.

questions.question: Which ID scheme gives roughly time-sortable 64-bit IDs without central coordination?
questions.explanation: UUIDv4 is random (poor index locality); UUIDv7/ULID are time-ordered 128-bit alternatives.

questions.question: List the 6 steps (with rough timings) of a 60-minute system design interview.
questions.answer: Requirements (0–8) → estimates (8–13) → API + data model (13–18) → high-level design, walking a request (18–30) → 2–3 deep dives (30–50) → wrap-up: bottlenecks, failures, monitoring, cost, v2 (50–60).

questions.question: Name 8 requirement questions to ask in every design.
questions.answer: Users and top use cases; out of scope; DAU and requests/user; read:write ratio; data size and growth; latency targets (p50/p99); consistency needs; availability target; geography/data residency; security/privacy/multi-tenancy.

questions.question: Explain leader–follower replication lag and two ways to give read-your-writes.
questions.answer: Async followers apply writes later, so a user can read stale data right after writing. Fixes: read from the leader for a short window after the user's write (or for that user's own data); use session/version tokens and route to a replica that has caught up.

questions.question: How do you handle a hot partition key?
questions.answer: Salt the key (key#0..key#N) and aggregate on read; cache it in front; split the hot entity; use a separate path for celebrities; rate limit abusive callers.

questions.question: Name 7 reliability patterns.
questions.answer: Timeouts; retries with exponential backoff + jitter; idempotency keys; circuit breakers; bulkheads; load shedding/backpressure; graceful degradation; health checks + autoscaling; canary/blue-green deploys; rate limiting.

questions.question: URL shortener: how do you generate keys without collisions or a single bottleneck?
questions.answer: Pre-allocate ID ranges to each app server from a coordinator (ZooKeeper/DB), base62-encode the counter; or hash + collision check. 7 base62 chars ≈ 3.5 trillion keys.

questions.question: Web crawler: name 4 hard parts.
questions.answer: Politeness (per-host queues, robots.txt, rate limits); URL dedupe (Bloom filter) and content dedupe (SimHash); crawler traps; recrawl scheduling by change rate; distributing by host hash; DNS caching.

questions.question: Payment system: name 4 must-haves.
questions.answer: Idempotency keys on every API; double-entry, append-only ledger; payment state machine; async PSP webhooks with retries; daily reconciliation; audit logs; saga + outbox for cross-service flows.
